content.name: Gregory Lindqvist
content.title: Lead Mechanical Engineer, PE
content.summary: Licensed Professional Engineer (Michigan) with 15 years designing thermal systems, powertrain components, hydraulics and robotic end-effectors. Leads a team of seven engineers on automation products, and a redesigned gripper platform cut unit cost by 21% while doubling rated cycle life.

experience.title: Mechanical Engineer I
bullets: Designed brazed aluminum heat exchanger cores in SolidWorks for commercial vehicle cooling modules.
Ran thermal and pressure-drop tests on a wind tunnel rig, correlating results with CFD to within 6%.
Released 120-plus drawings to production using ASME Y14.5 GD&T and the company's ECN process.

experience.title: Mechanical Engineer II
bullets: Owned the design of transmission pump housings from concept through PPAP for two automotive OEM programs.
Led DFMEA sessions with manufacturing and quality, closing 34 high-priority risks before launch.
Cut casting porosity scrap from 7.5% to 3% by working with the foundry on gating changes and wall-thickness tweaks.
Passed the PE exam and became licensed in Michigan in 2016.

experience.title: Senior Mechanical Engineer
bullets: Led mechanical design of a compact hydraulic power unit line rated up to 3,000 psi.
Ran FEA on manifolds and mounting brackets in ANSYS, removing 14% of material without lowering the safety factor.
Managed a $1.4 million development budget and a team of four engineers and two designers.
Brought the product to market four weeks ahead of schedule, reaching $6 million in first-year sales.

experience.title: Lead Mechanical Engineer
bullets: Lead a team of seven mechanical engineers designing grippers, end-effectors and safety guarding for industrial robots.
Redesigned the gripper platform around common modules, reducing unit cost by 21% and doubling rated cycle life to 10 million cycles.
Set up design review gates and a test lab plan that cut late engineering changes by about 40%.
Review and seal guarding and fixture calculations where customer contracts require a PE stamp.
Mentor two EIT engineers preparing for the PE exam and run quarterly GD&T training.
